title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. S is a category and S_ab its category of abelian group objects. C is a full additive subcategory of S_ab. A is a full subcategory of C such that every object of C is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of objects of A. Every X in S gives the functor h_X : M ↦ Hom_S(X, M) on C, which is additive. It is therefore determined by its restriction to A, a functor on the preadditive, non-additive category A. The heading '8° — Hom_{½-add}(A, Ab)' names this category of 'half-additive' functors on A. These are the additive functors on the preadditive A, whose additive hull recovers C.

This page specializes to S = Δ̂ = Ss (simplicial sets; '½ simplicial' is the old French 'semi-simplicial' = simplicial). It treats two cases.

Case 1°.
- C is the category of strictly ∂-perfect simplicial abelian groups. Via Dold–Kan these correspond to bounded complexes of finitely generated free Z-modules.
- A consists of the 'elementary' objects: Φ(i,n) (n ≥ 1, i ≥ 1) and the T-objects indexed by j ≥ 0.
- Natural reading: Φ(i,n) = F(Z --n--> Z), placed in degrees i and i−1, and T^j = F(Z[j]), where F is the Dold–Kan functor.
- Smith normal form for each differential gives the decomposition. Over the PID Z, kernels of maps between finitely generated free modules are direct summands. Hence every bounded complex of finitely generated free abelian groups is isomorphic (not merely quasi-isomorphic) to a direct sum of Z[j]'s and (Z --n--> Z)'s.
- n = 1 gives the contractible pieces; '∂-réduit' means none of these occur.
- So the functor M ↦ Hom_Δ̂(X, M), for M ∂-reduced, is equivalent to the data φ ↦ Hom_Δ̂(X, Fφ) for φ in A.
- Concretely:
  - Hom(X, F(Z[j])) = Z^j(X; Z), the normalized integral j-cocycles.
  - Hom(X, F(Z --n--> Z)) is the set of cochains c in C^{i−1}(X; Z) with δc divisible by n. This is cochain-level mod-n Bockstein data.
  - The morphisms of A (multiplication by integers, reductions, Bockstein-type maps) act on these.
- Hence the whole functor is recovered from the integral cochain complex C*(X; Z). The next page states exactly this.
- He adds a variant A_0 'without dimension', with φ running over objects L^i.

Case 2°.
- A subcategory C_0 of 'special' simplicial abelian groups, with torsion-free homotopy groups.
- A_0 ⊂ C_0 is formed by objects L^i = Λ̇L_n (i ≥ 1) and Ψ^j = Λ̇T_n (j ≥ 0).
- Λ̇ is some construction he does not define here. A marginal note says C_0 is additive but lacks some further property (reading uncertain).

Purpose. The next page makes the aim explicit. Knowing h_X on perfect coefficients is the same as knowing C*(X, k), for k Dedekind. The real goal is to reconstruct, as extra structure on the cochain complex, the multiplicative data:
- F(M) ⊗ F(N) → F(M ⊗ N) (cup products);
- Γ^i F(M) → F(Γ^i M) (divided powers).
In short: an integral or Dedekind-ring cochain model of the homotopy type, with products and divided powers, encoded as a functor on simplicial coefficient modules.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The 'isomorphic to a direct sum of elementary objects' claim requires finitely generated free (or projective over a PID or Dedekind ring) bounded complexes and Smith normal form. The 'strictly ∂-perfect' hypothesis presumably secures this.
Including n = 1 in Φ(i,n) (n ∈ N*) adds contractible objects. This is harmless but redundant once M is assumed ∂-reduced.
Case 2° is fragmentary: the functor Λ̇ and the exact definition of 'spéciaux' are not given on this page.

ideas.what: Recovering the representable functor M ↦ Hom_Δ̂(X, M) on perfect simplicial abelian groups from its restriction to a generating subcategory of elementary Eilenberg–MacLane/Moore-type objects (functors on a preadditive category versus its additive hull).
ideas.modern_name: Additive (Cauchy/additive-hull) extension; Dold–Kan; Smith normal form decomposition of perfect complexes over a PID
ideas.where_published: Similar functor-of-coefficients viewpoints appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs; not this specific setup

ideas.what: Hom(X, F(Z --n--> Z)) is identified with integral cochains whose coboundary is divisible by n, i.e. a cochain-level encoding of Z/n-cohomology and Bocksteins. So h_X on perfect coefficients is equivalent to the integral cochain complex C*(X; Z).
ideas.modern_name: Cochains as a corepresented functor on simplicial modules

ideas.what: Programme, made explicit on the next page: encode the homotopy type via the functor of coefficients together with multiplicative structure (cup products, divided powers Γ^i) on integral cochains.
ideas.modern_name: E∞/divided-power cochain models of integral homotopy types; affine stacks / schematization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mandell (E∞ cochains, 2001/2006); Toën (Champs affines, 2006); Grothendieck's schematization in Pursuing Stacks (1983)
ideas.where_published: Schematization of homotopy types discussed in Pursuing Stacks (1983); the 1975–76 cochain/divided-power version unsure

missed.claim: Around 1975–76 Grothendieck sets up the reconstruction of integral (Dedekind-ring) homotopy-type data as the functor M ↦ Hom_Δ̂(X, M) on perfect simplicial modules. This functor is shown equivalent to the cochain complex, with a view to adding cup products and divided powers. This anticipates both his own 1983 schematization ideas and Toën's affine stacks and Mandell-type integral E∞ cochain models.
missed.quote: On note que la connaissance des Hom_Δ̂(X_·, M_·) comme un foncteur en M_· ∂-réduit équivaut à celle de Hom_Δ̂(X_·, Fφ) pour φ dans A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This dates the 'homotopy type as functor on coefficient modules, with multiplicative/divided-power structure' viewpoint to the mid-1970s. It is relevant to the history of integral models of homotopy types. Mathematically this page is only the linear setup.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine linear reduction: perfect complexes over Z split into elementary pieces, so the functor is the cochain complex. Its interest lies in the dated programme it serves (integral cochain models with divided powers, a precursor of schematization and affine stacks). That aim is already signalled by the dossier title, and the later literature developed it independently.
transcription_corrections: 'sh. ∂-parfaits' is more likely 'st. ∂-parfaits' (strictement ∂-parfaits), matching 'sth./str. parfaits' on the next page.
In 1°, the second family of objects appears in the image as a Λ̇-type symbol applied to T_n (indexed by j ≥ 0), as in 2°; it is not 'Ť_n'.
The interlinear insertion reads approximately 'X_· ∈ Ob Δ̂ [fixé?]', specifying the fixed simplicial set X.
The left marginal note beside 1°, read as 'C étoilé[?]', looks more like 'C dilatée[?]' / 'C dilaté'; uncertain.
The left marginal note beside 2° reads roughly 'C_0 est additive mais non ... [stable par facteurs directs? / karoubienne?]'; the second adjective is uncertain, but it is not 'additive'.
In 2° the parenthetical reads roughly '(dont les ... ∈ C et les π_i(...) sans torsion)'.
